title: Combining genotypic and phenotypic analyses on single mutant zebrafish larvae
author: Dupret, Völkel, et al.
materials: 1.Boil the samples 10 min at 95 °C2.Load the protein samples onto a SDS denaturating gel (NuPAGE, 4–12% Bis-Tris polyacrylamide gel, Invitrogen) and run for about 90 min at constant 150 V3.Transfer the proteins to a nitrocellulose membrane by iBlot Gel Transfer Stacks (Invitrogen) at 20 V for 7 min (preset program P3)4.Block the membrane by incubation in Blocking Buffer, 1 h on an orbital shaker. Alternatively, membranes could be blocked overnight at 4 °C5.Incubate the membrane with the primary antibody in Blocking Buffer for 1 h at room temperature. The incubation of the membrane with the antibody is performed by spreading the antibody solution with a pipette on the membrane, placed onto a Parafilm M flattened on the bench6.Wash the membrane 3 times 10 min in PBST7.Incubate the membrane with the secondary antibody in Blocking Buffer for 1 h at room temperature8.Wash the membrane 3 times 10 min in PBST9.Visualize the protein using a chemiluminescence substrate (Super Signal West Femto, Thermo) and a Luminescent Image Analyzer (LAS-4000, Fujifilm).

steps.title: Anesthetize larvae in MS‑222
steps.instruction: Place zebrafish embryos or larvae in 6‑well plates containing MS‑222 anesthetic solution (300 mg L⁻¹) until fully sedated.

steps.title: Transfer sedated larvae
steps.instruction: Using a P20 micropipettor with a cut‑off tip, move each sedated larva into a 10‑cm Petri dish that also contains MS‑222 solution.

steps.title: Tail (or spinal cord) transection
steps.instruction: Under a stereomicroscope, cut the tail distal to the intestine (or cut the spinal cord just after the blood vessel within the pigment gap) with a sterile scalpel to obtain a tail biopsy while preserving the anterior body for downstream analyses.

steps.title: Separate tail biopsy and anterior part
steps.instruction: Transfer the tail tip into a 0.2 mL sterile tube for DNA work; place the remaining anterior portion into a 24‑well dish containing MS‑222 overdose solution (300 mg L⁻¹) on ice for euthanasia.

steps.title: Extract genomic DNA from tail
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL 50 mM NaOH to the tail biopsy, heat at 95 °C for 20 min, cool at 4 °C for ≥15 min, then neutralize with 1 µL 1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 7.4), vortex and briefly centrifuge.

steps.title: Fix and embed anterior part for histology
steps.instruction: Remove excess MS‑222, add 1.5 mL 4 % PFA and fix overnight at 4 °C; wash 5 min with PBS; transfer to glass pillboxes; dehydrate through ethanol series (30 %, 50 %, 70 % 10 min each, then 100 % 15 min); infiltrate with 50 % ethanol/50 % Claral 10 min RT, then 100 % Claral 15 min RT; fill pillboxes with pre‑warmed paraffin at 58 °C overnight, incubate twice 15 min at 58 °C; embed in stainless‑steel molds, orient, solidify 30 min at 58 °C, 1 h at 37 °C, then RT overnight; cool ≥4 h at 4 °C, trim paraffin, attach block to larger block, section at 5 µm, place sections on a water drop on a glass slide, dry 5 min at 37 °C, then 30 min‑1 h at 37 °C, and store slides ≥1 night at 37 °C.

substeps.instruction: Remove MS‑222, add 1.5 mL 4 % PFA; fix overnight 4 °C.
Wash once with PBS for 5 min.
Dehydrate: 10 min each in 30 %, 50 %, 70 % ethanol; 15 min in 100 % ethanol.
Infiltrate: 10 min in 50 % ethanol + 50 % Claral (RT); 15 min in 100 % Claral (RT).
Paraffin infiltration: overnight at 58 °C, then two 15 min incubations at 58 °C.
Embed in molds, orient, solidify: 30 min 58 °C, 1 h 37 °C, then RT overnight.
Cool ≥4 h at 4 °C, trim, attach to larger block, section 5 µm.
Place sections on water drop, dry 5 min 37 °C, then 30 min‑1 h 37 °C, store ≥1 night 37 °C.

steps.title: Extract total protein from anterior part
steps.instruction: Add 7.5 µL 1× Laemmli buffer to the frozen anterior tissue, mash ≥20 times, add another 7.5 µL 1× Laemmli buffer, mash again, boil 1 min, centrifuge 10 min at 20 800 g, 4 °C, and keep the supernatant at –80 °C.

steps.title: Extract histones (optional)
steps.instruction: Add 7.5 µL Triton Extraction Buffer (TEB) to frozen tissue, mash ≥20 times, keep on ice 10 min, centrifuge 10 min at 20 800 g, 4 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 7.5 µL TEB, centrifuge again, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 7.5 µL 0.2 N HCl, extract overnight at 4 °C on a rocker, centrifuge 10 min at 20 800 g, 4 °C, keep supernatant at –20 °C, add 3.75 µL 4× Loading buffer, 1.5 µL 10× Reducing Agent and bring volume to 15 µL with 0.2 N HCl.

steps.title: Perform Western blot
steps.instruction: Boil protein samples 10 min at 95 °C; load onto a 4–12 % Bis‑Tris gel and run ~90 min at 150 V; transfer to nitrocellulose with iBlot at 20 V for 7 min (program P3); block 1 h in Blocking Buffer on a shaker (or overnight 4 °C); incubate primary antibody 1 h RT (apply on Parafilm); wash 3 × 10 min PBST; incubate secondary antibody 1 h RT; wash 3 × 10 min PBST; detect with SuperSignal West Femto substrate and image on LAS‑4000.

steps.title: Extract RNA from anterior part
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL Trizol to the frozen anterior tissue, snap‑freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C ≥1 night; on ice, mash with pestle, rinse pestle with 100 µL Trizol, vortex 15 s, incubate 5 min RT, centrifuge 15 s at 20 800 g, add 60 µL chloroform, vortex 15 s, incubate 3 min RT, centrifuge 20 min at 14 000 rpm (≈20 817 g) 4 °C, transfer ~100 µL aqueous phase, purify with RNeasy Mini Kit (including on‑column DNase), elute in 14 µL RNase‑free water.

steps.title: Reverse transcribe RNA
steps.instruction: Combine 7 µL RNA, 10 µL RT Reaction Mix, 2 µL RT Enzyme Mix and 1 µL DEPC‑treated water (20 µL total); mix gently, incubate 10 min at 25 °C, 30 min at 50 °C, 5 min at 85 °C, place on ice, add 1 µL RNase H, incubate 20 min at 37 °C, then store cDNA at –20 °C.

steps.title: Amplify cDNA by PCR
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL cDNA, 2.5 µL 10× Polymerase Buffer, 0.5 µL 10 mM dNTPs, 2.5 µL 25 mM MgCl₂, 0.5 µL each primer (10 µM), 0.5 µL Taq DNA Polymerase (5 U µL⁻¹) and 13 µL water (25 µL total); run PCR: 95 °C 4 min; 35 cycles of 95 °C 45 s, 55 °C 45 s, 72 °C 1 min; final extension 72 °C 10 min; add 4 µL Loading Buffer and resolve on 1 % agarose gel in TAE.

steps.title: Spinal cord transection and regeneration assay
steps.instruction: Anesthetize 3‑dpf embryos in MS‑222 (300 mg L⁻¹) in 6‑well plates, transfer to a 10‑cm dish with MS‑222, cut the spinal cord just after the blood vessel within the pigment gap using a sterile scalpel, collect the tail tip for DNA extraction as described earlier, then place embryos in a 24‑well plate containing tank water with 1× Penicillin‑Streptomycin; monitor spinal cord regeneration for 2 days post‑amputation and genotype tail biopsies by RFLP if desired.

description: Forwardand reverse genetics in zebrafish has established a huge variety of mutants [[1], [2], [3], [4], [5]]. Since numerous mutations are homozygous lethal at early developmental stages, methods allowing both genotyping and phenotype analyses of mutant zebrafish embryos and larvae are required. The method is designed to investigate the phenotype of sibling zebrafish larvae from heterozygous zebrafish incrosses. As so, single zebrafish larvae must be genotyped in order to eventually establish a correlation between different phenotypes and distinct genotypes. After transection, the larval tail is used for genotyping, whereas phenotypic studies are performed on the anterior part of the zebrafish larvae.
